subject: Integration constraints: SSO/KMS/log retention - next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@lumenhealth.ai>, procurement@lumenhealth.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment constraints and immediate asks

Hi Claire / Lumen team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call highlights (as we heard them)
- Primary preference: private deployment or dedicated capacity depending on KMS/HSM and long-term logging needs.
- Identity: Okta SAML required for employee SSO; SCIM provisioning would be a plus.
- Keys: Customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys (AWS KMS with CloudHSM or equivalent) is a requirement for data-at-rest encryption of model artifacts and keys.
- Logging/retention: regulatory-driven retention target ~10 years for audit logs (state-level requirement), custody of logs must be auditable and exportable.
- Network: VPC peering / private connectivity is expected; some workloads may need on-prem access later.

High-level implications
- Hosted API (shared) is only viable if we can support a private VPC and customer-managed KMS/HSM — we flagged that as atypical for shared hosting but possible with Dedicated/Private variants.
- Redwood Dedicated gives predictable throughput and can be configured with customer KMS and private networking; Private VPC (customer-managed control plane) is the least friction for your compliance needs.

Please confirm the following so we can advise the right path (Private vs Dedicated):
1) Confirm the exact KMS provider and whether a CloudHSM-backed key is mandatory.
2) Is full custody of key material required (we can support BYOK workflows)?
3) Confirm the legal retention window for logs and whether logs must be retained on your side or can be retained in a customer-managed S3/GCS bucket.

Attachments: I attached a draft SOW and our security evidence checklist to speed procurement review.

Next steps
- If you confirm KMS/HSM and retention details, Marcus (solutions) and I will put together a target architecture diagram and a one-hour technical workshop with your infra team.
- If the retention requirement is firm, we should scope Private VPC in the SOW and mark Dedicated as contingent.

Thanks — available for a quick follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

Cheers,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Claire Huang <claire@lumenhealth.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment constraints and immediate asks

Thanks Avery — great recap. Quick answers below and a couple of additional asks from procurement:

Answers to clarifying Qs:
- KMS/HSM: We require AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys. Customer must be able to rotate keys; Redwood must be able to use customer-managed keys on the model serving instances.
- Key custody: Yes, keys must be under our control (BYOK).
- Log retention: Our compliance team requires 10 years of immutable audit logs for model access and admin operations. Logs should be stored in our S3 with MFA-delete or equivalent.

Procurement asks:
- Please provide a security architecture diagram showing where customer KMS keys are mounted and how logs are exported to customer S3.
- Can Redwood provide SOC2 evidence and a KMS/HSM integration checklist (we may need a brief technical statement for Legal).

Constraints:
- Hosted shared endpoints are not acceptable unless they fully support VPC isolation + BYOK KMS. If that is not possible, we expect either Redwood Dedicated or a Private deployment.

Happy to take the architecture diagram and a short technical note on the KMS workflow. Also, we need to carve out time for our infra team for an hour-long technical workshop next week (preferably 5/25 or 5/26).

Best,
Claire Huang
Director, Infrastructure Security | Lumen Health
claire@lumenhealth.ai

Internal notes / recommendations:
- KMS/HSM: CloudHSM + KMS BYOK is non-negotiable. We'll need to validate our KMS integration path: support for AWS KMS with external key material import or a KMS proxy that allows customer keys to be used on dedicated instances. Marcus, can you confirm the exact integration pattern we recommend (KMS proxy vs. prisoner-agent on host)?
- Logs: 10-year immutable retention -> we should map to an export path to customer S3 with lifecycle rules. Monica, can you validate if our log export tooling supports S3 with MFA-delete/immutability?
- Network: This pushes strongly to Private VPC or Dedicated with a customer VPC peering + routing policies. Private is probably cleaner for compliance-heavy customers; Dedicated may be acceptable if we can demonstrate BYOK + VPC isolation in the SOW.

Action items
1) Marcus: produce a simple 1-page architecture diagram showing KMS integration options (KMS proxy vs agent) and the log export flow. Due: 5/21 EOD.
2) Monica: confirm log export technical fit and list any gaps for immutable retention. Due: 5/21 EOD.
3) Karthik: draft a short SOW clause for Private deployment and for Dedicated fallback (we'll provide both options). Due: 5/21 EOD.

I'll coordinate scheduling the technical workshop for 5/25 or 5/26 once we have the diagram.

Thanks,
Avery
